**PREMISE CORRECTION 1 (the survey wording was unexecutable; the orchestrator
ruled at groom).** The AC draft asked that "each report's timestamp/tree-hash
field post-dates the merged t84 commit". Four of the five tools emit no
timestamp and no tree hash at all: gitleaks writes a bare JSON array,
semgrep writes a `results`/`paths` object, and pip-audit and npm-audit write
plain text. Hand-stamping a tool output to satisfy a fence is fabrication, and
a refresh card is exactly the place where that must never happen. So ac1
measures per-tool freshness instead of one impossible field:

- trivy DOES carry an internal `CreatedAt`, and ac1 requires it strictly later
  than `git show -s --format=%ct 67c9db975d75e0e6ae53667c02318a54c2524912`
  (measured at groom: `2026-10-17T03:20:21.362788969+08:00`, epoch 1792178421,
  against the base commit time 1792176563).
- semgrep is proven fresh by EXTRACTION rather than assertion:
  `backend/app/telemetry.py` merged at t78, AFTER the committed report was cut,
  and it is ABSENT from the committed reports 580 `paths.scanned` entries
  (measured). A refreshed report that does not list it in `paths.scanned` is
  the stale report. The refreshed sweep scanned 883 paths.
- gitleaks, pip-audit and npm-audit have no internal time at all. Their
  currency rests on the pinned reference sweep
  (`docs/state/outputs/t86_scan_run.json`), the per-tool blob-diff floor in
  ac5, and the count delta in ac3.

**DISCLOSED LIMIT (stated the way t84 stated the metrics gap).** For
gitleaks, pip-audit and npm-audit an identical-content re-run is
indistinguishable from a stale file - those tools simply do not write a time.
Their currency is therefore a conjunction (pinned reference count and exit
code + per-tool blob-diff floor + count delta), not a timestamp, and a
reviewer auditing "scan currency" for those three tools is auditing that
conjunction. This is a mechanism limit of the frozen tool set, disclosed here
rather than papered over with an authored timestamp field.

## Acceptance criteria

### ac1 - the five committed reports exist, parse, and are FRESH by per-tool measured evidence

Each JSON report parses under the stored-gate rules and each `.txt` report
carries its parsable summary line. Freshness is measured per tool, because
only trivy has a time to measure (the DISCLOSED LIMIT above): the trivy
`CreatedAt` must be strictly later than the base commit time read with
`git show -s --format=%ct 67c9db975d75e0e6ae53667c02318a54c2524912`; the
semgrep `paths.scanned` must include `backend/app/telemetry.py`, which merged
at t78 and is measurably absent from the committed reports 580 scanned paths;
the gitleaks report must parse as the tools own JSON array; and the reference
anchor must be present, name this base, and record a legal exit code for each
of the five legs. RED at base by design: at the base the five committed
reports describe the tree they were cut on - the trivy `CreatedAt` predates the
base commit time and telemetry.py is not in the scanned list - so ac1 is RED
before the refresh runs, not because a file is missing.

```bash
bash -c 'command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "ac1 RED: python3 is missing - a skipped probe proves nothing about a refreshed tree, so this fence fails loudly instead of skipping"; exit 1; }; D=$(mktemp -d); printf "" | base64 -d > "$D/t86_ac1_probe.py" || { echo "ac1 RED: the pinned t86_ac1_probe.py could not be materialised - report it, never edit the fence"; rm -rf "$D"; exit 1; }; python3 "$D/t86_ac1_probe.py" "$PWD" "$PWD/docs/state/outputs/t86_scan_run.json" || { echo "ac1 RED: the probe exited non-zero - its own ac1 RED lines above name the failing leg"; rm -rf "$D"; exit 1; }; rm -rf "$D"; echo "ac1 GREEN: THE FIVE REPORTS ARE FRESH BY MEASURED PER-TOOL EVIDENCE - the trivy CreatedAt is strictly later than the pinned BASE commit time, semgrep re-scanned the t78 telemetry module the base report never saw, both .txt summaries parse, and the reference anchor binds the timestamp-free tools (see the ac1 evidence lines above)"'
```

Whatever gitleaks measured, it must be committed unaltered, and it must have

any other file is builder dirt and is RED; every finding is the documented

**Named-path classification (the closed list ac2(iv) enforces).** A hit file
is accepted if `git cat-file -e BASE:<path>` succeeds, OR the path is one of:
`docs/issues/t86.md`, `docs/issues/groom/t86.md`, `docs/issues/closed/t86.md`,
`docs/state/outputs/t86_definer_groom.json`,
`docs/state/outputs/t86_builder_implement_BLOCKER.json`,
`docs/log/orchestrator_wal.jsonl`. The last is named by OWNERSHIP CLASS: the
orchestrators WAL is append-only, grows every WAL commit, and its prose quotes
the very false-positive pattern under discussion - it is not builder dirt and
never can be, and naming the PATH (never a line number) absorbs its unbounded
growth. The named set is CLOSED and adjudicated: a hit on any file that is
neither at BASE nor named is builder dirt and is RED (the negative control
bites exactly there). Measured classification of the builders prospective base
`a4d2a5e` (recorded in the grooms measurement log): 21 hits, 21/21 ACCEPT,
zero REJECT - 14 on BASE-existing files, 6 on named paths, 1 on the WAL. What
differs between the grooms tree and that base: the WAL, the builder BLOCKER
handoff (committed for the record; it carries the same false-positive prose
three times) and `docs/state/seq.txt` - no code, no dependency and no report
file differs, which is why the four code/dependency tools keep EXACT deltas
while only gitleaks needs the floor form. The anchor sits inside the swept
set, so the builder writes it from the first pass and re-runs the gitleaks
sweep with it present before committing: two passes, one story.

every number from bytes - the left half from `git show BASE:<report>`, the
right half from the committed reports. A number the card names that the parse
does not confirm is RED; a measured difference the card does not name is RED.
This is the t72 count-gate lesson inverted: the card REPORTS the new count, it
does not pin the old one.

draft assumed the criterion doc would be regenerated by this card if counts
drifted. The measurement says otherwise: the generator pins

`7ff2d65d90ae93e06dcab64c7bedb11eff5aa0a1`) and the generator script. The

  EQUALITY only, and that distinction is the disclosure, not a mitigation.
- The orchestrator records this merge with `regressions: 1 DISCLOSED` naming

### ac5 - delta purity: five reports, the reference anchor, and this cards own room - nothing else

The diff against the literal commit `67c9db975d75e0e6ae53667c02318a54c2524912`
(tracked AND untracked) may contain only: the five reports under `security/`,
the reference anchor `docs/state/outputs/t86_scan_run.json`, and this cards own
room (`docs/issues/t86.md`, `docs/issues/groom/t86.md`,
`docs/issues/closed/t86.md`, `docs/state/outputs/t86_*.json`, plus the groom
scratch dir `t86_scratch/`). Everything else is HARD RED, with no disclosed-
cause route: `docs/backlog.md` and `docs/state/merge_test_index.json` are the
orchestrators files; `docs/criteria/`, `Makefile`, `backend/`, `frontend/`,
`observability/`, `ops/`, `openapi.yaml`, `README.md`, `.github/`,
`docs/incident-response/` and every other `docs/` file belong to other cards or
to the frozen mechanism.

This leg is **BASE-pinned NON-APPENDABLE**: it compares against the literal
immutable sha `67c9db975d75e0e6ae53667c02318a54c2524912`, never `HEAD` and
never a moving ref, so it stays reproducible after this card merges; and the
allowlist above is CLOSED - a later card that needs a new purity path must
re-groom this card rather than widen the list from the outside. That is the
t73-t84 doctrine restated for this card, and it is why this leg is excluded
from the appended index like t73-t84 excluded theirs.

**ANCESTOR_YES disclosed-cause route (a disclosure, NOT a fence change).**
When this leg runs on a tree whose ANCESTOR merges already carry sibling-card
files (the builder verifies above the pinned BASE), the diff against the
literal BASE lists those ancestor paths and this leg goes RED on them -
measured on the builders BLOCKER run: `docs/issues/t85.md`,
`docs/issues/groom/t85.md`, `docs/log/orchestrator_wal.jsonl`,
`docs/state/seq.txt`, `docs/state/snapshot.json`,
`docs/state/outputs/phase_13_review_plan.json`,
`docs/state/outputs/t85_builder_implement.json` and
`docs/state/outputs/t85_definer_groom.json`. Those rows are ANCESTOR_YES: a
disclosed cause owned by the orchestrators merge bookkeeping, never a purity
claim about this cards own delta, and the orchestrator records them as such.
The fence bytes stay UNCHANGED for this, and the allowlist remains BASE-pinned
and NON-APPENDABLE; only this disclosure is added.


Two further legs make the floor specific rather than aggregate. First, the
per-tool blob-diff floor: EVERY one of the five reports must differ from its
BASE blob, and the trivy blob and the semgrep blob must EACH be shown to differ
explicitly - an aggregate "something changed" check would be satisfied by
either one alone, which is exactly how a half-refresh gets committed. The
measured sweep of this tree moved all five (gitleaks 0 -> the 12-hit BASE floor, semgrep 32 -> 33,
trivy a new `CreatedAt` and re-serialised payload, pip-audit the `python-jose`
advisory relabel, npm-audit the 23rd advisory), so byte equality for any tool
here means that leg never ran. Second, the
merge-order measurement: `ops/diagnosis.md` must be byte-clean against the base
- t86 lands before t85, so the tree this refresh pins is the tree before t85s
ops prose lands, and touching it here would both break that claim and collide
with t85s ADD-only append.

## Verification commands

ac_hash: sha256:c499d3e62558804a71c8e2b037e8e48fd2ea0d7a915bf1b1a642bb5a1efc0cc5

Five fenced commands, byte-identical to
`evidence.verification_commands.ac1..ac5` in
`docs/state/outputs/t86_definer_groom.json`. The digest is sha256 over the
`JSON.stringify` array of the five FENCED BLOCKS in ac1..ac5 order, each block
taken exactly as it sits between its ```bash fences (the `bash -c '...'`
wrapper INCLUDED) with COMPACT separators and each block CR-stripped and
trimmed - the t58/t62..t84 recipe, so the digest covers the command exactly as
it is pasted rather than a re-derived form. Recomputed from the card on disk by
the grooms assembler so the digest cannot drift from the card.

Each command is a deterministic single `bash -c` one-liner with exactly two
single quotes, no heredoc, no backtick, pure ASCII, run from the repository
root. The python probes travel as base64 literals materialised into a
`mktemp -d` scratch directory and are removed by the fence itself. Each fence
REDs loudly if `python3` is missing - a skipped probe proves nothing about a
refreshed tree, and a fence that skips is worse than a fence that fails. Every
probe pins the literal base sha internally, so a fence cannot be made green by
pointing it at a different commit.

**Measured protocol, in order, as run at groom.** ALL_RED at base
`67c9db975d75e0e6ae53667c02318a54c2524912` with the BASE reports in place (all
five fenced commands exit 1 for their named reasons - ac1 on the trivy
timestamp and the missing telemetry.py in `paths.scanned`, ac2 on the missing BASE
fingerprints and anchor disagreement, ac3 on the DELTA block, ac4 on the card text,

the pristine candidate restored byte-for-byte (all five exit 0); then the

## Constraints (hard)

- The product delta is SIX paths (the disclosed `max_files` exceedance above):
  `security/gitleaks-report.json`, `security/npm-audit-report.txt`,
  `security/pip-audit-report.txt`, `security/semgrep-report.json`,
  `security/trivy-report.json` and the reference anchor
  `docs/state/outputs/t86_scan_run.json`. Plus this cards own documentation
  room.
- The scan mechanism is FROZEN: same tools, same pinned versions (gitleaks
  v8.30.1, trivy v0.75.0, semgrep and pip-audit via `uvx`/`uv`), same t36
  gate-time allowlist construction, `Makefile` byte-clean. A refresh that makes
  a finding disappear by changing the mechanism is a FAIL, not a pass.
- No finding is dispositioned, edited away, or allowlisted by this card. The
  register/disposition loop is t87s job; this card reports what the tools
  measured. The 12 BASE gitleaks fingerprints and the 2 new loop ids in
  ac3 are t87s BINDING input and are carried verbatim in the groom handoff.
- The five reports must come from ONE sweep of ONE tree (the currency claim).
  If a tool cannot run, the builder reports that leg DEFERRED with the measured
  reason (the phase_7 deferral discipline - a deferred row is never written as
  PASS) rather than re-stamping the old report or hand-writing output.
- If a re-run count of the FOUR code/dependency tools differs from the
  reference anchor because the upstream advisory database moved, the builder
  reports the measured difference and STOPS for a re-groom. A gitleaks count
  difference is EXPECTED (its hit set is tree-relative): the builder
  regenerates the anchor from its own sweep instead. It never hand-edits a
  report, a pin or the anchor.
- No CI wiring (REQ-CICD-073 forbids scan jobs in CI); the refresh is run the
  way the phase_7 refresh was run - operator-side, committed output.
- No product-code, contract, ops-doc, observability or incident-response
  change; no dependency addition (the scans READ dependencies, they do not add
  them). `docs/criteria/security_ops_verification.md` and
  `backend/scripts/security_ops_verification.py` are NOT touched by this card
  (ac4); the hand-maintained criterion-13 prose is t89s territory.
